rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body L1-90 carries none. Maintainer block's dated notes (L93 Lean pass, L97 Emphasis pass, L99 Auto-load-check, L107 Save-then-diff) are the licensed provenance-header shape the rule itself carves out. L93's 'Lean pass (2026-08-25...): cut "..." + "..." ... Do not restore' matches the rule's own named exception verbatim: 'the licensed "Cut (date) ... Do not restore" accept-note carries it by design'. Harm the rule guards against (changelog-as-body, re-derivable history) is absent: nothing here narrates a transition in currently-live body prose, each note anchors a standing do-not-restore/do-not-add constraint.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L11 'STRIDE's value is rejection, not enumeration.' is a Rory-shaped counterintuitive reframe; L19-20 ('STRIDE is a six-category checklist...The subagent does the walk; you read the result.') is Boris-direct factual. Both land inside the AE101 voice quintet with no L&D-coach or motivational-poster register. No atmospheric/sensory imagery to scan, no `**Remember:**`-style wrapper, no valence-loaded metaphor keyword (cargo/theatre/ritual/tourist/poster), no negation-callout self-contradiction (no 'we refuse'/'we don't' callout present), no slang requiring the Godin-plausibility test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: STRIDE's originator attribution (Kohnfelder/Garg, Microsoft) lives correctly in the backing-block Sources with the cultural-vocabulary fallback noted there ('STRIDE is cultural vocabulary in security work') rather than owed inline. No 'Antti'/'the creator'/'the author' anywhere in body (grep over L1-90: zero hits). No first-person-plural author-we in body (author_we grep in view.json: 0 hits, CLEAN). Timing: L3 '**Time:** 20 minutes.' sits directly below H1, total-only, and sums correctly from the three phase timings (7+8+5=20).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.

'subagent' is earned functionally at first use (L20: 'The subagent does the walk; you read the result. It runs in fresh context against the map'). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.

If its six categories feel wrong for your feature (some features are really abuse-case or insider-threat shaped...) say so in the Alternatives considered section.' rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every section closer for dangling pronoun/demonstrative and vague spatial/temporal metaphor: L70 'Just tell Claude to move it over' — 'it' resolves singularly to 'the ADR' (only candidate antecedent in the two preceding sentences). L78 'ADRs accumulate, the window is finite' and L79's closer both have concrete referents. No bypass-the-agent punchline (no 'write that yourself'/'go fix it').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it (Antti-directed 2026-08-12, mandation removed from `curriculum/exercises/README.md`).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L87: '**What happened:** You made one call and wrote the ADR, and the decision shipped to the repo. The rest of the STRIDE output stayed in the session as evidence, not on disk.' This is 30 words, past tense throughout, and is the rule's own named calibration example: 'passes on move 3' is quoted verbatim in the compendium against this exact sentence. Count+noun (one call / the ADR), destination (shipped to the repo), no step-sequence replay.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All human-to-agent verbs are peer-flat or warmer: ask, tell, push back, work with, steer. No bark/order/command/whip/drag/boss verb present anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All nine section headers checked against their section's actual claim: none contain a spatial/structural metaphor contradicting the mechanism, and none use an 'other X'/'the rest of the X' with no primary designated.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L11's negation ('rejection, not enumeration') is earned against the reader's actual prior, not empty: the file's own backing-block Stance explicitly frames this as 'a slightly contrarian position against how STRIDE is usually taught' (enumeration-as-checklist is the default reading a professional would bring). No deictic drumroll ('That is the X.'), no bold-label echo beyond exempt widget chrome (**Time:**/**Window:**/etc., which restate a value, not a subject), no citation/appendix duplication (body carries no inline STRIDE-source gloss to duplicate against the backing block).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L19-20: 'STRIDE is a six-category checklist for threats. Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege. The curated skill walks your surface against all six, so you don't hold the taxonomy in your head.' 'all six' sits directly adjacent to the six-item enumeration it counts, the rule's cut-shape ('adjacent to the list -> cut'). Harm check: drift risk is effectively zero (the file's own Stance block calls STRIDE's six categories 'settled... older than most of the room' and 'not the part of this curriculum that moves'), so the only live harm is minor redundancy, not staleness. L64's later 'its six categories' is the legitimate memory-handle reuse (distant from the list, carried forward) and is correctly kept.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut 'all six' to 'against all of them' or drop the numeral entirely; the six-item list two clauses earlier already carries the count.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No superlative construction (only/always/never/nothing else/the one thing that) present anywhere in body — nothing for this rule to test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L29 'The output over-produces on purpose. You reject most of its entries in the next phase; that rejection is the point, not a failure of the scan.' is the survivor shape: concrete instance, then one generalising clause, then stop. No abstract-twin duplication, no restating of the adjacent fenced prompts (each body lead-in states only the prompt's opening move, per §38), no widening qualifier, no repeated second announcement within the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap phrasing ('you already think you're using X'), no ability-tier assumption ('at your scale', 'a senior would already know'), no unreachable identity-criterion (no tourist/practitioner split). The one pre-prompt verification gate present (P1's 'security-tools skill... pre-flight to verify the local environment is ready') is a genuinely new-to-this-gate variable (curated skill freshly invoked), plausibly failable, not a redundant recheck of an already-confirmed state.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'ADR (Architecture Decision Record)' and 'subagent' earned at first use as noted under check_writing §8. 'worktree'/'fork prompt'/'scrollback' are continuity vocabulary already established earlier in the M3 arc, not first-used cold here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.

Just tell Claude to move it over') and L30's 'if it comes back instant, push back and re-run' both satisfy the boundary test (plausible failure named + non-obvious rescue given) rather than violating the golden-path ban; these are the rule's own licensed exception, correctly applied, not troubleshooting exported to a maintainer-only surface. The below-the-fence 'View summary' field (L95) is the one named below-fence exception and ships correctly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Register throughout matches the file's own 'earned trust, deepening' mood target (maintainer Meta block); no bleed from another module's mood (no M1 joyful-creation register, no M5 sustained-unease register).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every read/check/push-back instruction has both an actor+mechanism and an object+tell (L46 'Read what Claude proposes. Push back if the story doesn't fit your codebase's reality.'; L54 'read the diff before you decide whether to keep it'; L63 'Read it. If it reads like it was written for a compliance reviewer rather than a future engineer, push back'; L68-70 addressee-explicit 'tell Claude to move it over'). But the *Name*-is-a-smell sub-clause fires twice: L36 'The move: name the worst realistic case first' and L79 'naming exactly what to read at the start of a long-running session' both use 'name/naming' as the primary instructional verb outside a prompt fence, trainer-note, or established coinage. Harm is real but mild (register precision, not a functional break): 'name' is vaguer than the swap and slightly under-specifies which move is being asked.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: L36: 'The move: write down the worst realistic case first' (or 'state'). L79: 'Selective load is the practitioner default: picking exactly what to read at the start of a long-running session, rather than trusting broad auto-load.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L69's '`pwd` would have answered differently' is explanatory (describing what the agent itself could have checked to reason correctly about location), not an instruction for the student to run `pwd` manually. The actual instruction given (L70) is 'tell Claude to move it over' -- forcing function stays in chat throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view.json greps.em_dash: 0 hits over body L1-90, CLEAN, planted_proof true. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.

rules_evaluated.fix_hint: L37: 'The agent drafts it; your read of your own codebase decides whether it's real.' -- matches 'The agent proposes' earlier in the same sentence.

'session' used correctly throughout for one sitting (L68 'your main session's repo', L78 'a future session loads them').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.

No premature-rescue or resolved-doubt wrong-edit present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.

H1 'Pick one threat, record the decision' names the deliverable. File is one of the 12 AE101 exercises already validated under this rule (2026-07-04 corpus pass, avg blind-squint 3.9/5).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four fences (threat-model-with-stride-1..4) checked via scripts/expand-md.js output: no `[BRACKETS]`-style placeholder in any of them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.

Find the access-surface map's path in this scrollback before dispatching') rather than an invented path. P3 uses the rule's own blessed fuzzy-fallback for first-create intent ('check for an existing docs/adr/ folder... if there isn't one, use docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 explicitly defers the pick ('Don't pick yet -- I'll decide next'), not pre-judging Phase 2's job; severity-flagging in P1 is scan-output structuring, not the worst-case incident judgment Phase 2 owns. P2 does not invoke any named skill or reference Phase 3's ADR-writing prematurely.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No `/clear` or 'start a new session' instruction in any of the four fences; all four assume continuous scrollback ('the previous exercise', 'we just made', 'we discussed').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
rules_evaluated.evidence: scripts/expand-md.js output shows plain text inside all four fences -- no `**`/`*` markdown markers, P3's 'Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives considered' uses plain slashes, not bold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 (L24) names roughly nine distinct sub-steps (pre-flight, invoke, subagent-isolate, save, flag, don't-pick, report-loaded, find-path-before-dispatch, confirm-file-used) and P3 (L58) names roughly seven (check-folder, fallback-path, ground Context, ground Decision, ground Consequences, ground Alternatives, save-then-diff) -- both well past the '4+ named sub-steps' structural trigger. Neither fence carries an in-fence 'No preamble.' suppressor, and no body primer naming the preamble + skim-past cue follows either fence. P2 (L41) also names exactly 4 sub-steps (propose/map/name/propose-shape) with no suppressor. Harm: Claude's narration of these multi-step asks can eat the top-of-response slot before the useful content, per the rule's own stated mechanism.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add 'No preamble.' as the last line inside P1 and P3's fences (P2 is borderline at exactly 4 steps and lower-risk), or add a one-line body primer after each fence naming the skim-past cue.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: Maintainer accept-note (L107, 'Save-then-diff (2026-08-26)') explicitly directs post-action reporting over a pre-save gate for this exact prompt, citing check_prompts §21: 'do not add a pre-save gate to the prompt.' A grill-before-save clause would add exactly the pre-save gate the note forbids.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P3 ends 'Save the ADR to that path, then show me the diff.' -- exact post-action-report shape, and matches the maintainer's L107 accept-note naming this rule directly. P1 also saves-then-reports ('Save the threat list...Report whether or not the stride skill loaded... tell me which file it used').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No absolute path or `cd` command in any fence. P3's `docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md` is a session-root-relative path per convention.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.

It runs in fresh context against the map, not the raw code.') already carries the plain-sentence explanation the rule requires, satisfying the 'unless surrounding setup already obvious' clause even though it precedes rather than follows the fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P3's ADR save has an explicit named reader in body before the save happens (L53: 'It is the artifact your CISO would actually read.'). P1's scratch-location save is the first stage of a two-stage save whose final consumer is named later in the same exercise (L85: 'Your CISO and the next engineer read what's on disk, not your scrollback.') before the session clears.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: scripts/expand-md.js confirms all four expand to the exact label '**Prompt**' (no custom suffix like 'Prompt: X').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: None of the four prompts opens with an interview pattern ('Ask me which files...'); all four go straight to the natural work request given what's already established in body/scrollback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's map-location logic ('Find the access-surface map's path in this scrollback before dispatching') is fully inside the fence, not relying on body callouts. P3's ADR-path fallback logic is likewise self-contained inside its own fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 is split into 5 paragraphs by move (pre-flight / invoke+isolate / save+flag / don't-pick+report / find-path+confirm). P3 is split into 3 paragraphs by move (convention+template / content-grounding / save+report). P2 stays one paragraph as a tightly-compounding sequential-build ('Start by...then...name...and propose...'), the rule's own licensed exception for that shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2's lead-in ('propose the most plausible incident story and walk you through the STRIDE pick') and P3's lead-in ('draft the ADR in your repo's convention, save it, and show you the diff') and P4's lead-in ('whether this ADR rides into future sessions automatically') all share verb + noun-phrase with their fence's opening clause. P1's lead-in ('invoke the STRIDE skill as a subagent') does NOT mirror its fence's actual opening move (the security-tools pre-flight) -- but this is the documented §38a surprise-pedagogy carve-out: the maintainer block's 'M3 supply-chain easter egg -- DO NOT SPOIL IN BODY' note (L101-105) names the prompt, the surprise mechanism, the reason the mirror is intentionally absent, and the trainer move, satisfying all four elements §38a requires of the accept-note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Session is warm throughout (no `/clear` between Ex1 and this file); P1 correctly handles the 40a concurrent-context wrinkle of its own subagent dispatch by resolving the map's path in the warm parent session BEFORE dispatching ('Find the access-surface map's path in this scrollback before dispatching'), rather than assuming the fresh-context subagent can resolve it itself. No 40b curriculum-coined label (e.g. a Phase-heading name) is referenced inside any fence as if it were in scrollback; P3's 'the hardening decision we just made' anchors to genuine prior-turn content.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's 'Don't pick yet' targets an action (picking a threat) not requested anywhere in this prompt, so it cannot block the earlier save instruction. P3 ends 'Save the ADR to that path, then show me the diff' with no STOP anywhere in the tail -- matches the rule's own blessed shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: Rule targets fix-pass editing behaviour (whether to strip a leading-looking line); this is a fresh read with no edit underway. P1's 'Don't pick yet -- I'll decide next' is the clearest load-bearing-guardrail candidate the rule describes, and it is correctly present, not stripped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P3's Context/Decision/Consequences/Alternatives-considered structure is specified because the ADR format IS the teaching moment (the rule's own named exception).
